title: fix(plugin-calendar,plugin-gantt): show a stored date-only day on that day and write a date field as the calendar day (objectui#10866, sites 1 and 2)
body:
Part of #10866

Clause-②: no
Every read goes through the existing `toDisplayDate`, and a write to a `date` field sends the spec's own `YYYY-MM-DD` storage form. No declared key, export or accept set moves. `@object-ui/types` changes one description string.

## What changed

This is slice 1 of the date-only zone family's successor card: sites 1 and 2, per triage `5861646819` item 1. It covers the calendar and the gantt, and in each plugin the reads and the writes change together. Sites 3 to 6 are later slices, listed under Acceptance notes.

**Reads: every stored date-only value now goes through `toDisplayDate` from `@object-ui/core`.** That function reads a date-only value at local midnight of the day it names. A value with a time keeps its instant.
- plugin-calendar `ObjectCalendar`: the event `start` and `end`.
- plugin-calendar `calendar-view` renderer: each event's `start` and `end`, and the authored `currentDate` (`resolveAuthoredCurrentDate`).
- plugin-gantt `ObjectGantt`: the task `start` and `end`, and `baselineStart` / `baselineEnd` (new helper `readTaskDate`).
- plugin-gantt `GanttView`: a marker's `date`, in both the zoned `markers` memo and `resolvedMarkers`, and the inline editor's committed start and end.

**Writes: a `date` field is written as the calendar day.** This covers the calendar drop (`handleEventDropDefault`), the calendar quick-create (`submitQuickCreate`) and the gantt drag (`handleTaskUpdateDefault`).
- A field declared `date` is written as the local calendar day `yyyy-MM-dd`, using core's `toDateInputValue`.
- Any other declared type (`datetime`) keeps `toISOString()`.
- With no object schema to ask, the stored value's own shape decides (`isRealCalendarDate`). That is the same split the read makes, so the read and the write cannot disagree.
- A quick-create has no stored value, so on a field with no declared type it still writes the instant.
- New private helper `toStoredDateValue`, one in each plugin.

**The gantt `timeZone`.** The card asked for a decision on `tzShift`'s treatment of a date-only value. The decision: a date-only day stands on that day of the chart's own calendar, for every viewer, and a drop writes the day of the chart's calendar it landed on.
- `GanttView` re-bases every `Date` it is handed into the business zone, and translates every emitted change back.
- `ObjectGantt` therefore hands it the instant that re-bases onto the named day's local midnight (`readTaskDate`). It reads a drop back through the same shim before taking the local day (`toStoredDateValue`).
- A date-only marker is placed on its day and is not re-based.
- With no `timeZone` both halves are the identity. That is the showcase's case and every chart's default.
- Two alternatives were not taken:
  - A per-task "this is a day" flag on `GanttTask` would widen an exported type (a public face, Clause-② yes).
  - Leaving days re-based like instants puts the bar on the previous day for any viewer east of the chart's zone.

**The gantt working calendar (`skipWeekends` / `holidays`, `scheduling.ts`).** The scheduler floored to UTC midnight and keyed days with `getUTCDay` / `toISOString()`. That only agreed with a date-only value while the value was read as UTC midnight.
- It now floors to local midnight and steps by calendar day. It keys days the way `GanttView`'s own column fold (`isWorkingColumn`) already did.
- Left on UTC, a rescheduled successor landed a day early in every zone except UTC (see H1).

**Also moved:**
- `makeTzShift` moved unchanged out of `GanttView.tsx` into a new `plugin-gantt/src/tzShift.ts`, and `GanttView` re-exports it. The reason is that `ObjectGantt` now calls it, and the `ObjectGantt` suites replace `./GanttView` with a probe (`vi.mock('./GanttView', …)`). Imported from there, it was undefined in each of those suites: the first full run went red with `No "makeTzShift" export is defined on the "./GanttView" mock`.
- Two `ObjectGantt.test.tsx` cases pinned the defect. They expected a drag to write `2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z` into a field declared `date` (on the api provider, a field stored as `2024-01-01`). They now expect `2024-02-01`. Both carry a comment saying so.
- `@object-ui/types`: the `holidays` JSDoc and its zod `.describe()` said the keys were UTC days. This change made that false, so both now say calendar days on the chart's own calendar. This is an in-place fix under the bounded exemption:
  - It is the same defect class, a one-phrase fix.
  - No open PR touches `objectql.ts` or `objectql.zod.ts`. I read the open-PR file lists at 2026-09-28T02:18Z and again at 03:11Z; the only file hit anywhere near this change is the release PR's CHANGELOGs.
  - It uses the same gate family.
  - The changeset names `@object-ui/types` as a `patch` for it.

**Fix round 1, at `687890effa`.** CI on `8ac7b62270` went red in `Test (shard 7/8)` on the objectui#9909 locale census (`machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`). The contract review on that commit asked for three more changes.
- **The census entry follows the shim.** Moving `makeTzShift` also moved a DECLARED site: `tzOffsetMs`'s `en-US` `formatToParts` parser, which never renders text. The census reported `GanttView.tsx · new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { — declared 1, found 0` and an undeclared `[en-US]` site in `tzShift.ts`. That `DECLARED` entry now names `packages/plugin-gantt/src/tzShift.ts`. Its expression, count (1), verdict and reason are unchanged. The root `vitest.config.mts` comment that cited `tzOffsetMs` by its file is re-pointed the same way.
- **Literal-anchor sweep of the move.** I grepped tests, scripts and ledgers for `GanttView.tsx` together with `makeTzShift`, `tzOffsetMs` or `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US'`. The census entry and that config comment were the only hits. The other `GanttView.tsx` ledgers (`residue-namespaces-3546`, `gantt-count-interpolation-4157`, `check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`) name i18n keys and union types, which did not move.
- **`GanttViewProps.workingCalendar` (exported).** Its JSDoc still said `holidays` were UTC keys. It now says they are calendar-day keys read on the chart's own calendar: the viewer's, or the business `timeZone`'s when one is set.
- **Other UTC working-day rule sites.** I swept plugin-gantt, plugin-calendar, types, `content/docs` and `skills` for UTC wording about holidays, weekends or working days. Two more encoded the retired rule, and both now read the local day:
  - `scheduling.test.ts`'s weekend count (`getUTCDay`). It is equivalent under the suite's pinned `TZ=UTC`.
  - `packages/plugin-gantt/scripts/verify-phase6b.mjs`'s weekend-start check. This is a manual Playwright script, not run by CI; its browser context sets no `timezoneId`, so the page and the script share one zone.
- **Changeset.** The Writes bullet now ends: a calendar quick-create has no stored value, so there it still writes the instant. The frontmatter is byte-identical.
- **Files this round:** `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`, `vitest.config.mts` (comment), `packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx` (JSDoc), `packages/plugin-gantt/src/scheduling.test.ts`, `packages/plugin-gantt/scripts/verify-phase6b.mjs` and `.changeset/10866-calendar-gantt-date-only-days.md`.

## H1 and H2

**H1, measured on base.** The new pins were added over the base source (`b93e245f9`, source unchanged) and run in the objectui#10183 driver's forks child. Controls, west = `America/Los_Angeles`, east = `Asia/Shanghai`:
- **Calendar, west.** `2026-10-05` sat in the `October 4, 2026` cell. A two-day move wrote `'2026-10-07T00:00:00.000Z'`. A quick-create on the 12th wrote `'2026-10-12T07:00:00.000Z'`.
- **Calendar, east.** The read was already right. A move wrote `'2026-10-07T00:00:00.000Z'`. A quick-create on the 12th wrote `'2026-10-11T16:00:00.000Z'`, which names the 11th.
- **`calendar-view`, west.** `currentDate: '2026-11-01'` opened on October, and `2026-11-05` sat on the 4th.
- **Gantt reads.** The task start read as year, month, day, hour `[2026, 10, 4, 17]` west and `[2026, 10, 5, 8]` east.
- **Gantt writes.** A drag wrote `toISOString()` instants into both `date` fields.
- **Zoned charts.** A west viewer of a chart zoned `Asia/Shanghai` got the bar at `[2026, 10, 5, 8]`. An east viewer of a chart zoned `America/Los_Angeles` got `[2026, 10, 4, 17]`.
- **Markers.** A `2026-10-05` marker stood 32 px (west) and 37 px (east) off the edge of a bar starting that day.
- **Inline editor.** A typed `2026-10-07` was committed as `[2026, 10, 6, 17]` west and `[2026, 10, 7, 8]` east.
- **Working calendar.** A successor of a Friday task landed at `[2026, 10, 11, 17]` (a Sunday) west, and at `[2026, 10, 9, 8]` (the Friday itself) east.
- **`datetime` controls, green on base and on head.** The instant `2026-10-06T04:00:00.000Z` sits on its local day in each zone. A two-day move writes `2026-10-08T04:00:00.000Z` in both zones, and a gantt drag keeps the instant.

**H2, the census.** It covers the non-test sources of both plugins, searching for `new Date(`, `toISOString(` and `Date.parse(`. Neither plugin imports a date-fns parse. Each site is classified by the field it serves.

Date-only (a stored `Field.date` value, or an authored day). All are fixed here:
- `ObjectCalendar`: event start and end; drop patch; quick-create payload.
- `calendar-view` renderer: event start and end; `currentDate`.
- `ObjectGantt`: task start and end; baselines; drag patch.
- `GanttView`: marker date, 2 sites; inline editor start and end.
- `scheduling.ts`: the UTC day key and the UTC floor.

Datetime, or not a stored value, and so left as is:
- `ObjectGantt`: the tooltip's datetime sniff, which is a validity check on a datetime-shaped string. The `new Date()` placeholder for a date-less record. The `lockedRange` min/max copies.
- `CalendarView`: every `new Date(x)` copies a `Date`. Its props are typed `Date`, and the day math uses local getters and multi-argument constructors.
- `GanttView`: the `tzShift` shim, `now()`, copies and arithmetic. The `startDate` / `endDate` props are typed `Date`.
- `calendar-view` renderer: the registry's sample events (demo data built from `new Date()`).
- `ResourceWorkload`, `shifts.ts`, and the rest of `scheduling.ts`: copies and millisecond arithmetic.
- `ObjectCalendar`: the clock (`useState(new Date())`, `handleCreate`).

## Pins and ablation

**Five new pins, registered in the objectui#10183 driver's `PINS`.**
- `ObjectCalendar.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: the read cell, a two-day move and a quick-create, with `datetime` controls.
- `calendarViewRenderer.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: events and `currentDate`.
- `ObjectGantt.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: reads with baselines, the drag payload, and a zoned chart read and written, with `datetime` controls.
- `GanttView.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: markers, unzoned and zoned, and the inline editor.
- `scheduling.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.ts`: the weekend and a holiday.

How the pins run:
- Each zone opens with a rig case.
- The suite-zone cases also run in the normal run. They assert the written shape, which UTC can tell apart.

**Red on base, green on head.** On base the driver gave `Tests 6 failed | 8 passed (14)`: all 5 new pin rows plus the child-exit row, and the 8 existing pins stayed green. The failed cases were:
- every date-only read case, west, plus the east gantt read and markers;
- every date-only write case, both zones;
- both zoned-chart cases;
- both inline-editor cases;
- all 4 working-calendar cases.

The rigs and the `datetime` controls passed.

**Ablation (read routing reverted), at `f9ae4ebd7b`.** I committed first, then used `ablation-replace.mjs --hold` with 10 anchors, each asserted `x1 → x0` with a changed blob. They set every read above back to `new Date(…)`: 2 in `ObjectCalendar`, 3 in the `calendar-view` renderer, 1 in `readTaskDate`, and 4 in `GanttView`. No `dist` is involved: the vitest root config resolves `@object-ui/*` to `src`, and the plugin files are imported relatively. The driver went `Tests 5 failed | 9 passed (14)`.
- **Red:** the calendar read (west), the `calendar-view` read (west), the gantt read in both zones, both zoned-chart cases, and all 4 marker cases and both inline-editor cases.
- **Green:** every pure write case, meaning the gantt drag onto the 7th in both zones, all quick-creates, and the calendar east move. All `datetime` controls and the working calendar also stayed green.
- **One write row reddened, as a cascade: the west calendar move.** It moves the event two days from the cell it was drawn in, so with the read reverted it wrote `'2026-10-06'`. That is still a day, not an instant, just one day early.
- **Restore.** Each file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` to its HEAD blob (`68688411c93a`, `26454aa22622`, `266f62c9ecdb`, `257811400efc`), and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

## Serial

- **Claim.** The earliest live `Claim:` on the card is `5861874880` (seat 2, this PR). A later claim, `5861881966` (seat 4, site 1 only), names branch `claude/issue-10866-calendar-date-only`. That branch did not exist on the remote when this one was cut, and nothing here touches it.
- **Open PRs.** At 2026-09-28T02:18Z and again at 03:11Z, no open PR touched `packages/plugin-calendar`, `packages/plugin-gantt`, `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` or the zone-pin driver, apart from the release PR's CHANGELOG and `package.json` lines.
- **Merge order.** The next slices of #10866 register in the same `PINS` list, so they are serial after this PR.

## Acceptance notes

**#10866 remains open; sites 3 to 6 are later slices.**
- `plugin-timeline`: `ObjectTimeline.dateBucket`, the sort, the renderer's `formatDate` default face and the axis extent.
- `plugin-charts`: `AdvancedChartImpl.formatTick` and its `toISOString()` fallback.
- Core `FormulaFunctions`: `DATEADD` / `DATEDIFF` / `DATEFORMAT` against `TODAY()` / `NOW()`. Triage requires one zone decision, measured against the server formula engine.
- The i18n helpers: `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, `formatRelativeTime` and `formatDateSpec`.

**Observed, not filed.** Each is a read-only inference, not measured.
- **Calendar drop across a DST change.** `CalendarView`'s move adds the millisecond delta between two local midnights to the event's start. Suppose an event starts on the 25-hour day (the first Sunday of November, west), and is grabbed from a later cell of its span. The new start then lands at 23:00 of the day before the target, and a `date` field is written as that day. This is pre-existing arithmetic: a `datetime` event moves by an hour on the same path.
- **Business-zone day placement near DST.** It inherits `makeTzShift`'s per-instant offsets, which the shim documents as close rather than exact near a DST transition in either zone.
- **Date-only end is exclusive.** A date-only gantt end reads as that day's start, so the bar ends where the end day begins. This is unchanged by this PR.
